description.narrative: (i) increasing agricultural productivity in project area (ii) more economic use of irrigation resources through change of farmers' and Land Reclamation Agency's (LRA) behaviors.

Despite the current pricing and subsidy mechanisms, which do not encourage economic irrigation, the central issue of Romania's irrigation sector today, remain that irrigation facilities will likely become economic as the agriculture sector redevelops in the coming years. The primary objectives of the project are to achieve, and increase the economic use of irrigation though changes the Land Reclamation Agency's (LRA's) behavior, to increase agricultural productivity in the project area. Through the following components, the project will: 1) rehabilitate main distribution systems in two stages, within which the schemes to be rehabilitated would be chosen based on the likely long-term economic viability. The criteria for schemes selection are: static pumping head (less than 70m), advanced state of water user associations (WUAs) development, and system transfer, strong demand, secure water sources, and, no environmental, nor social impediments; 2) support institutional reform in land reclamation, specifically through technical assistance (TA) and equipment to develop an appropriate management information system (MIS) system, supported by international and national specialists, for the Land Reclamation Agency (LRA) staff. In addition, TA will support the preparation of a business, and asset disposal plan, focusing on those elements with commercial potential. The component will also support the Land Reclamation Directorate within the Ministry of Agriculture - MAFWE - by assisting with the development of procedures to review service charges, and performance monitoring, and, in developing a database for monitoring WUAs development. Further training and TA will be provided to WUAs; 3) support technologies for reducing energy consumption for irrigation, through a technical study that confirm its economic and financial viability. Technical specifications and procurement documents will be prepared; and, 4) provide project management support in procurement issues, monitoring and evaluation, and issues of financial management, institutional restructuring, and engineering.

title.narrative: Maintenance cost per volume of water delivered to users in project area

baseline.value: 153 US$ per 1000 cum delivered to users

target.value: 45 US$ per 1000 cum delivered to users

actual.value: 10.3 $ per 1000 cum delivered to users

comment.narrative: The expenditure for maintenance is likely to increase after the users understood the effect of low maintenance on water delivery.The WUOs agreed to substantially increase the maintenance tariffs for 2012. However, meeting the target would take more time thantheremaining project life.

title.narrative: Maintenance cost per volume of water delivered to users in project area

baseline.value: 153 US$ per 1000 cum delivered to users

target.value: 45 US$ per 1000 cum delivered to users

actual.value: For 2011 irrigation season, the maintenance cost was 10.2 US$ per 1000 cum delivered to users

comment.narrative: This very low value is not a sign of increased efficiency or demand for water but clear proof of deferred maintenance of bothpublic and WUO infrastructure. Normal maintenance activities need to be restored. Target unlikely to be met given the lack ofstandardized maintenance activities and farmers reluctance to pay for regular maintenance.

title.narrative: Maintenance cost per volume of water delivered to users in project area

baseline.value: Actual expenditure of 153 US$ per 1000 cum delivered to users

target.value: 45 US$ per 1000 cum delivered to users

comment.narrative: Target not met because the expenditure is not likely to secure long-term functionality of the infrastructure.

actual.value: The expenditure for maintenance of the public irrigation infrastructure was 10.3 $/1000 cum delivered to users in 2011.

comment.narrative: The expenditure for maintenance is still much below the estimated cost of associated with regular maintenance activities to securelong-term functionality of the irrigation infrastructure (canals and pump stations). However, it is likely that expenditure formaintenance to gradually increase towards meeting the reasonable costs, once the farmers started understanding the risks of newdepreciation of the rehabilitated infrastructure. The maintenance tariffs for 2012 increased. Meeting the target would take moretime than the remaining project life.

comment.narrative: The target not met. The target was set without assessment of the likely impact of subsidy termination, hence, overestimated.
